_note: Quiz and true-or-false items written but not yet blind-checked; apply_check.py moves checked items onto the site.

item.statement: Indica and sativa labels show which smell compounds a weed has.
item.why: In 41,201 US lab-tested samples, the labels barely matched the terpene mix. The labels came from a strain website, and effects weren't measured.

item.statement: Sativa and indica strains differ mostly in their THC.
item.why: In one small Dutch study, a sativa-type and an indica-type coffee-shop strain had similar THC but different terpenes. That's two strains, not a rule.

item.statement: Confronting someone as a family works best to get them into treatment.
item.why: In one trial, 30 in 100 relatives started treatment after confrontation training, against 64 in 100 after CRAFT skills training. Seven in 10 families never held the confrontation.

item.statement: Family members only feel better if their loved one starts treatment.
item.why: In one trial, family members felt less depressed and angry in every group, whether or not the relative started treatment. With no group left without help, no approach can take the credit.

item.statement: In a survey, most festival-goers said sniffer dogs would stop them using drugs.
item.why: With dogs, 66 in 100 still said they'd use drugs, against 77 with no police. These were answers to made-up scenarios, not real behaviour.

item.statement: Benzo withdrawal can feel like the anxiety or sleep problems the pills were for.
item.why: Both reviews say withdrawal symptoms can resemble the original problem. They are expert reviews, so this is second-hand.

item.statement: Reviews that warn of seizures after stopping benzos say how often they happen.
item.why: Both reviews read warn of seizures, but neither gives a rate. The only count is 2 of 11 prisoners in 1961, in conditions unlike usual use.
